$schema_note: Canonical roster. lib/holdings.js and scripts/make_pdf.py both read this; edit here only.

positions.name: Global X Uranium ETF
positions.factor_role: The purest listed claim on the fuel bottleneck. Holds miners and enrichers, so it captures the spot uranium move with equity beta stacked on top.
positions.falsification_metric: A restart of idled Kazakh and Namibian supply, or one high-profile reactor incident, resets sentiment far faster than mine supply can respond.

memo.name: Global X Uranium ETF
memo.rationale: Nuclear is the fastest-permitting large-scale answer to hyperscaler 24/7 power demand; the broadest, most liquid way to hold exposure to the fuel cycle.

positions.name: VanEck Uranium & Nuclear ETF
positions.factor_role: Deliberately the boring half of the fuel pair. Weighted toward utilities and reactor builders rather than juniors, it earns cash while URA takes the risk.
positions.falsification_metric: It is not really a uranium proxy — the utility weighting means it can drift with rates while the actual fuel thesis plays out.

memo.name: VanEck Uranium & Nuclear ETF
memo.rationale: Deliberate overlap with URA on the nuclear theme rather than diversifying away from it. Conviction is high enough to accept concentration in exchange for broader coverage across the fuel cycle and regulated utilities.

positions.name: Petrobras PN
positions.factor_role: Pre-salt barrels at a single-digit multiple with a double-digit payout. Priced for permanent political risk, which is a real risk that is nonetheless already in the number.
positions.falsification_metric: Dividend policy is set by the controlling shareholder, and the controlling shareholder is the state. Fuel-price intervention ahead of an election ends the thesis without warning.

memo.name: Petrobras
memo.rationale: A large, cash-generative conventional producer as a hedge against nuclear permitting delays: thermal generation remains the marginal supplier during interim grid deficits.

positions.name: Saudi Aramco
positions.factor_role: The lowest-cost barrel on earth and the swing producer that sets the floor. Owned as the stabiliser of the bucket, not for its growth.
positions.falsification_metric: Free float is thin and the payout leans on the state budget. A sustained sub-$60 Brent forces a choice between the dividend and Vision 2030.

memo.name: Saudi Aramco
memo.rationale: Same logic as PETR4.SA with a different sovereign and cost-curve position; diversifies the conventional-energy leg across geography rather than concentrating it in one producer.

positions.name: LandBridge Company
positions.factor_role: The hinge of the whole book. Owns Permian surface acreage and collects royalties on whatever sits on it — water handling, pipelines, and now data-centre leases. Sells energy and compute demand without drilling or buying a GPU.
positions.falsification_metric: Small float, and the data-centre revenue is a handful of contracts. Concentration cuts both ways: it fell 9.5% in a single session on 12 Aug 2026.

memo.name: LandBridge Company
memo.rationale: Surface and water rights exposure in the Permian Basin: a direct read on interconnection-queue monetization and data-centre land-siting, the physical layer underneath the generation names.

positions.name: Nebius Group
positions.factor_role: A neocloud: rents GPU capacity by the hour to firms that will not build their own. Sits in this bucket because the binding constraint on the business is contracted power and shell space, not chips.
positions.falsification_metric: Classified here as a power consumer, which is a stretch — it is really a compute landlord. Capex-funded, customer-concentrated, and competing with hyperscalers who own their own silicon.

memo.name: Nebius Group
memo.rationale: Classified here as a power consumer, which is a stretch I flag rather than hide: Nebius is a compute landlord: capex-funded, customer-concentrated, and competing with the hyperscalers it sells to. It sits in Energy because its unit economics are gated by power access, not because it generates power.

positions.name: CoreWeave
positions.factor_role: The scaled version of the same trade as NBIS, with a contracted backlog rather than a spot book. The clearest listed read on whether AI capacity is genuinely pre-sold.
positions.falsification_metric: Debt-funded purchases of an asset that depreciates on a chip cycle. One anchor customer renegotiating resets the whole model, and it overlaps heavily with NBIS — this is one position expressed twice.

memo.name: CoreWeave
memo.rationale: Same classification stretch as NBIS, and the two overlap enough operationally that this is closer to one position expressed twice than two independent bets (see Section 4).

positions.name: Taiwan Semiconductor
positions.factor_role: The actual bottleneck. Nearly every accelerator in this book is fabricated by one company, so this is the least substitutable position in the portfolio.
positions.falsification_metric: A Taiwan Strait event is not a drawdown, it is a permanent impairment — and the same event takes ^KS11 and 2357.TW with it. The single largest correlated risk here.

memo.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing
memo.rationale: The central foundry bottleneck and the counterweight the thesis has to survive: near-monopoly on advanced-node and CoWoS packaging capacity captures the demand growth directly if the rotation thesis is wrong or early.

positions.name: Advanced Micro Devices
positions.factor_role: The only credible second source of accelerators. Owned as the option on buyers refusing to accept a single supplier, not as a bet on it winning outright.
positions.falsification_metric: The moat is software, not silicon. If CUDA holds, competitive hardware still does not convert into share, and the share gains are already in the multiple.

memo.name: Advanced Micro Devices
memo.rationale: Second-source accelerator exposure, kept smaller than a conviction bet would be: this bucket is insurance against the thesis, not a parallel thesis of its own.

positions.name: Palantir Technologies
positions.factor_role: The application layer. Sells the deployment of models into government and commercial workflows, which is where the margin sits once inference is a commodity.
positions.falsification_metric: The multiple is the position. Growth is real and accelerating, but at this valuation a single decelerating quarter costs more than the growth adds.

memo.name: Palantir Technologies
memo.rationale: Software/deployment-layer exposure, included so the bucket is not pure hardware and does not miss the demand side entirely.

positions.name: Vanguard Information Technology ETF
positions.factor_role: Broad exposure to the complex, so the bucket survives being wrong about any single name.
positions.falsification_metric: It already holds AMD, TSM's peers and the megacaps, so it overlaps with half this bucket. It dilutes single-name risk without adding a new bet — closer to a cash proxy with tech beta than genuine diversification.

memo.name: Vanguard Information Technology ETF
memo.rationale: A broad, low-conviction sleeve that keeps the bucket from being a handful of single-name bets on a theme this book is intentionally underweighting.

positions.name: ASUSTeK Computer
positions.factor_role: AI server exposure at a hardware multiple rather than a semiconductor one. The AI server business is repricing the whole company while it is still classified as a PC maker.
positions.falsification_metric: Server assembly is margin-thin with real customer concentration, and the legacy PC cycle still swamps the AI line in reported revenue.

memo.name: ASUSTeK Computer
memo.rationale: Server assembly exposure: margin-thin and customer-concentrated, and the legacy PC cycle still outweighs the AI server line in reported revenue. Held as a read on physical assembly capacity, not a pure AI-server bet.

positions.name: KOSPI Composite
positions.factor_role: Country-level exposure to memory. HBM pricing runs through Korean national accounts, and the index carries a persistent governance discount that is finally being addressed.
positions.falsification_metric: Not directly investable — it is an index, so a real book expresses it through a fund or futures and eats tracking error and FX.

memo.name: KOSPI Composite Index
memo.rationale: An index proxy for Korea's memory manufacturing exposure to the buildout, avoiding having to pick between the two dominant memory makers.

positions.name: iShares AI Infrastructure UCITS ETF
positions.factor_role: Spreads the infrastructure bet across semis, cloud and networking, including names the single-name lines here miss.
positions.falsification_metric: Overlaps with VGT and with the megacap complex most portfolios already own, and the LSE line quotes GBP against a USD NAV — an FX layer sitting on top of the actual exposure.

memo.name: AI Infrastructure UCITS ETF (LSE)
memo.rationale: A packaged, diversified sleeve of infrastructure and connectivity names as a lower-maintenance complement to the single-name bets elsewhere in the bucket.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.factor_role: The hedge against the financing of everything above. If the buildout is funded by deficits and suppressed real rates, gold is the direct expression of that — and as spot-backed shares it carries no expiry and no roll.
positions.falsification_metric: Pays nothing to hold. A genuine real-rate spike is its enemy, and it can fall alongside risk assets in a liquidity event precisely when the hedge is needed.

memo.name: SPDR Gold Shares
memo.rationale: Classic drawdown hedge, uncorrelated to the CapEx cycle either way. Held to reduce portfolio volatility, not to express a view.

positions.name: Avantis International Small Cap Value ETF
positions.factor_role: The deliberate opposite of the rest of the book: ex-US, small, cheap, profitable, and largely unowned by the AI trade. Here to be uncorrelated, not to be exciting.
positions.falsification_metric: Value has underperformed growth for most of a decade. If the buildout simply keeps compounding, this is a permanent drag.

memo.name: Avantis Intl Small Cap Value ETF
memo.rationale: Deliberately away from the AI theme entirely: developed-market, value-tilted, small-cap exposure as a genuine diversifier rather than a disguised extra bet on the same trade.

positions.name: JPMorgan Chase
positions.factor_role: The lender to the buildout. Captures capital-markets activity and a steeper curve without taking a view on which operator wins.
positions.falsification_metric: Imperfect ballast: it is levered to the same economy the rest of the book needs, so it fails in the scenario the hedge exists for. A credit cycle hits it and the neoclouds together.

memo.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
memo.rationale: A quality financial with real exposure to the debt financing the CapEx cycle runs on, but broad enough not to live or die on it.

positions.name: Investo MVIS Global Rare Earth & Strategic Metals
positions.factor_role: The materials upstream of everything else here: magnets, motors, turbines. Exposure to export controls on rare earths, which is the supply chokepoint the compute bucket cannot design around.
positions.falsification_metric: This is not ballast. It is a concentrated, policy-driven, high-beta commodity-equity basket that will likely fall with the rest of the book rather than against it — and it is a thin BRL listing carrying currency risk on top.

memo.name: Rare Earths / Critical Minerals ETF
memo.rationale: The other classification stretch I flag openly: a concentrated, policy-driven basket that tracks the same technology-materials cycle as the rest of the book, so in most states it does less true ballasting than its bucket label implies. The exception is an export-control shock, where it is the one line in the book that re-rates upward. It also traded in only about {coverage} of the measured window, which limits how much its long-horizon return figures should be trusted.
